---
title: Write safely
description: Change an item without overwriting someone else's change, handle a conflict when one happens, create an item only once, and retry a write without making it twice.
---

Another app or device may change an item after you read it. Marfa can tell, as long as your write names the **version** it read. [Versions](/versions) explains what the version counts and why Marfa works this way. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## Send the version you read

Read the item, change what you need, and send back the `version` you read with the properties you changed:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 3 --prop body="Start with the essays, then the letters."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 3, "properties": { "body": "Start with the essays, then the letters." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: { version: 3, properties: { body: "Start with the essays, then the letters." } },
});
```

An update **must name a version**: Marfa refuses one without it with `400 missing_required_field`, because it can't tell such a write from a blind overwrite. The properties you send are laid over the item's own, so send **only what you changed**. [Update an item](/api-reference/items/updateItem) lists the other fields an update takes.

Marfa answers in one of three ways:

- `200` with the item at the next version, when nobody changed it since you read it.
- `200` with the item further along, when someone changed it but not the fields you changed. Marfa applied your change over theirs, so replace your copy with the item in the answer: it holds both.
- `409 version_conflict`, when a field you changed was also changed since. The next two sections handle it.

## Resolve a conflict yourself

A conflict leaves the choice **with you**. `current` is the item as it is now, `ancestor` is the item at the version you read, and `conflicting_fields` lists the fields both writes changed.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Read the refusal

Here another app changed the note's body after you read version 3:

```json title="Response" status="409"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "version_conflict",
    "status": 409,
    "message": "Version 3 is stale; current version is 4. Conflicting fields: body."
  },
  "current": {
    "version": 4,
    "properties": { "title": "Reading list", "body": "Start with the letters." }
  },
  "ancestor": {
    "version": 3,
    "properties": { "title": "Reading list", "body": "Start with the essays." }
  },
  "conflicting_fields": ["body"]
}
```

In the TypeScript SDK, the refusal comes back as `error`, with `error.error.code` set to `version_conflict`. The CLI prints the conflicting fields and exits with status 1.

</Step>
<Step>

### Decide each value

For each field in `conflicting_fields`, compare your value with the one in `ancestor` and the one in `current`, and choose what to keep: combine the two, keep one, or show both to the person. A conflict can name `tier`, `occurred_at`, `source_id` or `type` as well as properties.

</Step>
<Step>

### Send it again at the current version

Send the value you chose, naming the version in `current`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 4 --prop body="Start with the letters, then the essays."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 4, "properties": { "body": "Start with the letters, then the essays." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: { version: 4, properties: { body: "Start with the letters, then the essays." } },
});
```

If someone writes again first, Marfa answers the same way. After a few tries, **show the person the conflict**.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Let Marfa resolve it

Add `conflict=auto`, and Marfa **settles each colliding field** by the item type's merge policy instead of refusing the write:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 3 --conflict auto --prop body="Start with the essays, then the letters."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>?conflict=auto
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 3, "properties": { "body": "Start with the essays, then the letters." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id }, query: { conflict: "auto" } },
  body: { version: 3, properties: { body: "Start with the essays, then the letters." } },
});
```

A type's [merge policy](/catalog/your-own-types#merge-policy) gives each field one of two strategies. `last_writer_wins` takes your value. `keep_both_copies` keeps the value the item holds now and writes yours to a conflicted copy. The copy is a new item of the same type, tagged `conflicted-copy`, with a `derived-from` edge to the original.

`core.note` **keeps both copies of its `body` and `notes`**, and takes the last writer for everything else.

The answer is `200` with the item, and beside it `conflict_resolution` says what Marfa did:

```json
{
  "fields": ["body"],
  "strategy": { "body": "keep_both_copies" },
  "conflicted_copy_id": "01a12312-394e-75d2-acdd-d19c6d58a423"
}
```

`conflicted_copy_id` is the **only place** the copy's `id` appears, so keep the `id` or show the person the copy. A write that collides on nothing carries no `conflict_resolution`. Marfa doesn't resolve a write that collides and also moves the item to another type: it answers `409 version_conflict`, and you resolve it yourself.

Apps built with the Swift SDK, and the CLI's `device` commands, write through a working copy that always asks Marfa to resolve. [Devices](/devices) explains how a device writes.

## When Marfa no longer holds your version

Marfa compares a stale write against its snapshot of the version you read. Snapshots are **thinned as they age**, so a long-held edit can name a version Marfa no longer has. Marfa then answers `409 ancestor_unavailable`, whatever `conflict` the write names, with the item as it is now in `current` and the version you sent in `requested_version`.

Make your change again **on top of `current`**, and send it at the version `current` holds. Sending your old values at the new version overwrites whatever arrived since.

## Create an item only once

A create that names a `source_id` an item already holds under its source **updates that item**, and a create that repeats an `id` answers the stored item. To create an item or change nothing, as an agent that may repeat a create should, add `mode: "create_only"`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.note --source-id reading-list --create-only --prop title="Reading list"
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "core.note", "source_id": "reading-list", "mode": "create_only", "properties": { "title": "Reading list" } }
```

If an item holds the `source_id` or the `id`, live or in the bin, Marfa **writes nothing** and answers `409 item_exists`, with the item's ID in `details.existing_id` and `source_id` or `id` in `details.matched_by`. The `source_id` decides when both match. [Upsert items in bulk](/api-reference/items/bulkUpsertItems) takes the same `mode` and reports such an entry `skipped`. To change that item, read it and [send the version you read](#send-the-version-you-read).

A key that can't read the item's type learns nothing about it: a `source_id` match answers `403 type_not_permitted`, and an `id` match `409 conflict`.

## Retry with an Idempotency-Key

When you don't know whether a write landed, because the connection dropped or Marfa answered `503 write_contention` or `429 rate_limited`, send it again. Give each write an `Idempotency-Key` header holding a fresh unique value, such as a UUID, and **use the same key when you retry it**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 3 --idempotency-key 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d \
  --prop body="Start with the essays, then the letters."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Idempotency-Key: 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 3, "properties": { "body": "Start with the essays, then the letters." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

const key = randomUUID();
const send = () =>
  marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
    params: { path: { id }, header: { "Idempotency-Key": key } },
    body: { version: 3, properties: { body: "Start with the essays, then the letters." } },
  });
```

If Marfa already answered that request, it returns the first answer again, with the header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and writes nothing. A repeat of a request refused `409 version_conflict` gets the same `409`. A repeat of one that failed with a `5xx` runs again.

A key names **one request**. The same key on another request, such as the resolved write after a conflict, answers `422 idempotency_key_reused` and writes nothing, so send each new write under a new key. A repeat that arrives while the first is still running answers `409 idempotency_key_in_flight`: wait, then send it again. [Errors](/api-reference/errors#retrying) says which refusals to retry.

The item operations that write one item, the edge, folder and view write operations, and [Apply a bulk action](/api-reference/bulk-actions/applyBulkAction) take a key.

### Rare replay answers

- A request refused `404 blob_not_found` keeps no answer, so the same key works once you upload the bytes.
- Marfa keeps only the **status** of a first answer larger than 1,048,576 bytes. A repeat writes nothing and answers `422 idempotency_result_not_retained`, with that status in `details.original_status`. A `2xx` status there means the first write landed.

The contract holds the rules: [versions](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/versions.md), [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#idempotency-keys) and [errors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/errors.md#errorsidem-not-retained).
